name: BlueBird Capital

terms.couponNote: 15% preferred, CUMULATIVE, paid before any return of capital and before the GP takes carry. The PPM reserves distribution timing to the GP’s discretion and says it expects to reinvest net revenues — but the GP has confirmed directly that the plan is to pay it ANNUALLY, which is how the model treats it.
terms.holdNote: Fund term is 7 years, extendable by the GP at its sole discretion for two successive one-year periods, so up to 9.
terms.sponsorMoicNote: Target 2.65x MOIC and a 20% gross IRR, from the investor deck.
terms.mgmtFeeNote: 2% annual management fee to the General Partner.
terms.carryNote: The waterfall is: 15% preferred first, then 100% return of LP capital, then GP carried interest of 90% with 10% to the LP. The GP takes nothing until capital and the full accrued preferred are paid — but above that line the split is heavily to the GP, so an LP’s realistic outcome sits close to capital plus preferred. Worth reading against the 2.65x target, which needs a large gross result to reach through a 90/10 back end.
terms.minimumNote: $100,000 minimum commitment, subject to GP discretion.

structure: A roll-up. The fund acquires several small, profitable gutter and roofing businesses across multiple markets and combines them into one cohesive operation, then exits by selling that platform to a private equity or strategic buyer. So it buys many companies but sells ONE — which is why it is modelled as a single exit event rather than a fund selling down over several years.
_about: Global deal facts only. Terms are identical for everyone who bought the same deal, so they live here rather than being retyped by each holder. Nothing personal is in this file: your commitment, funding dates, thesis and notes stay in your own tracker and never leave your machine.
source: PPM of Bluebird Capital Group, LP (January 2025), the First Call investor deck and the January 2026 Last Call pitch deck.
singleCompanyNote: Several acquisitions, one platform, one exit. The deal count is not what matters here; the exit being a single trade sale is.
